# Genuine critical caps obstruct lossless effective-profile gluing
transferring the sharp ORDINARY effective-cap-count profile unchanged
across an integer segment. It retains one set of original ambient
halfspaces, their affine thresholds, actual Minkowski compatibility,
strictly nonheavy fibers, and true global critical activity.

The one-dimensional three-interval maximum is already contained in
`candidate 5048c7e97ca98aef`. The additional ingredient
here is an exact paired-tail bound, which proves preservation of that
maximum under arbitrary centrally symmetric continuous product factors.
This permits genuinely critical continuous normals of rank two and
gives a sharp numerical test of the newly proved ordinary three-cap
profile. No below-OC counterexample or general OC implication is claimed.

## 1. Exact three-interval paired-tail lemma

For L>0 put

    T_L(t)=min(2L,max(0,L-t)),
    D_L(x,r)=T_L(r-x)-T_L(r+x),     r>=0.

Thus T_L is the upper-tail length of [-L,L]. The function D_L is odd
in x, and for almost every x its derivative is

    partial_x D_L(x,r)
      =1_{|x-r|<L}+1_{|x+r|<L}.                         (1)

It is therefore nondecreasing and 2-Lipschitz in x.

Fix l>0 and c>=0. Put the intervals [-l,l],[-l,l+4c],[-l,l] at
bases -1,0,1 respectively. Their total length is

    M_0=6l+4c.

For a real slope a, let G_a(s) be the mass of the actual ambient cap

    {x-c+a z>=s}

on those three intervals. Then, for every a in R and r>=0,

    M_0-2c <= G_a(r)+G_a(-r) <= M_0+2c.                (2)

**Proof.** The relative center of the middle interval is c, and its
half-length is R=l+2c. The endpoint relative centers are a-c and
-a-c. The identity T_L(-t)=2L-T_L(t) gives

    G_a(r)+G_a(-r)-M_0
       =D_R(c,r)-[D_l(a+c,r)-D_l(a-c,r)].               (3)

Write the bracket as Delta. By (1),

    0<=Delta<=4c,       0<=D_R(c,r)<=2c.

The upper bound in (2) follows immediately. If r<=l+c=R-c, both
thresholds in D_R lie in its linear range and D_R(c,r)=2c;
then (3) is at least -2c. If r>l+c, the two intervals supporting
the derivative in (1) for L=l have gap 2(r-l)>2c. The integration
interval [a-c,a+c], of length 2c, meets at most one of those two
open intervals. Hence Delta<=2c, again proving the lower bound.
Endpoints of those intervals are irrelevant to their length, so the
argument includes equality of all thresholds. This proves (2).

The lemma is an exact simultaneous estimate for every original
integer slope a and both threshold shifts. It does not independently
optimize unrelated endpoint caps or replace the integer sum by an
integral over real bases.

## 2. Exact mixed maximum after symmetric continuous padding

Let d>=1, let 0<=c<=l, and, when d>=2, let L be any centrally
symmetric convex body in R^(d-1), centered at zero, of volume V>0.
For d=1 omit L and set V=1. Define the actual convex body

    C={ (z,x,w): -1<=z<=1,
                   -l<=x<=l+4c(1-|z|), w in L }.

Its upper x endpoint is concave in z, so C is convex. It is compact
and full-dimensional. Its integer fibers are exactly the three
interval products specified above. Their mixed d-volumes are

    2l V, (2l+4c)V, 2l V,
    M=(6l+4c)V.                                        (4)

In particular their endpoint Minkowski average is actually contained
in the middle fiber. The point y=(0,c,0) is an actual middle-fiber
point. The maximum raw ambient halfspace depth is exactly

    B=(3l+c)V,
    max depth=B/M=(3l+c)/(6l+4c).                       (5)

**All-halfspace lower bound.** Move any containing cap parallel to
itself until its boundary passes through y; this only decreases its
mass. If its x coefficient is nonzero, normalize its sign and absolute
value. For positive x coefficient its section at w is an upper cap
of the form defining G_a, with threshold a linear functional of w.
Central symmetry of L pairs w and -w with identical volume element.
The lower bound in (2) therefore gives mass at least

    (M_0-2c)V/2=(3l+c)V.

For negative x coefficient use the complementary lower tails.
Every x-boundary has zero interval length, so their paired mass is
2M_0-[G_a(r)+G_a(-r)]. The upper bound in (2) gives the same lower
bound B. The absolute value r of the linear threshold suffices,
because (2) pairs both signs.

If the x coefficient is zero, the cap depends only on (z,w).
The corresponding projected measure has equal endpoint weights 2lV,
middle weight (2l+4c)V, and is invariant under (z,w)->(-z,-w).
Every closed through-origin halfspace therefore has at least M/2>=B.
This branch includes purely integer caps with a whole boundary fiber;
no boundary mass is removed from that argument. Thus every closed
ambient containing halfspace at y has mass at least B.

**Exact original-cap upper cover.** First, the following unperturbed
three caps suffice for every d:

    H_0={x>=c},   H_+={x<=c+A z},   H_-={x<=c-A z},

with A>l+c. Their affine margins L_0=x-c, L_+=c+Az-x,
L_-=c-Az-x obey 2L_0+L_++L_-=0. Consequently the three caps cover
the entire ambient space. The cap H_0 takes endpoint lengths l-c
and middle length l+3c. Each other cap takes one full endpoint of
length 2l, no positive volume from the other, and middle length l+c.
Every cap therefore has mass B. This proves the global upper bound
in (5), and all three caps are genuinely critical at y.

## 3. Critical continuous-normal rank two without changing any budget

Suppose d>=2. Choose a nonzero continuous functional v on the w-space
and epsilon>0 so that

    epsilon R_L<l+c,  where R_L=max_{w in L}|v(w)|.

Choose A>l+c+epsilon R_L, and replace the last two caps by

    H_+={x<=c+A z+epsilon v(w)},
    H_-={x<=c-A z-epsilon v(w)}.                        (6)

Their endpoints remain respectively full and empty. On the middle
fiber, both moving thresholds stay strictly between -l and l+4c.
Their mean retained length is l+c because the mean of v(w) on L is
zero. Thus all three ORIGINAL GLOBAL cap masses are still exactly B.
Their positive margin relation is unchanged, and all three boundaries
pass through y. By the preceding all-halfspace lower bound they are
truly active critical caps, rather than merely an equal-budget cover.
Their continuous normals span dimension two.

The cover is irredundant on the actual mixed set. At the middle base
take w=0 and x>c to obtain a point only in H_0. At the plus endpoint
take w=0 and x<c, for example x=-l/2 when c>=0, to obtain a point
only in H_+. The minus endpoint similarly witnesses H_-. These
points satisfy the displayed strict margins with the stated A.

For c<l/2, ALL three fibers are strictly lighter than M/2. Indeed
the only potentially largest one has mass (2l+4c)V, and

    (2l+4c)V<M/2  iff  c<l/2.                          (7)

Thus none of the following failure depends on a heavy fiber or a
rank-one continuous cap family.

## 4. Exact failure of the ordinary effective-three-cap profile

For an ordinary uniform convex body of dimension at least two, the
audited effective-cap-count theorem gives, for a three-cap cover,

    sum_(i=0,+,-)(A_i-alpha)_+ + alpha/Gamma_2 >= M,
    Gamma_2=4/9.                                      (8)

This statement cannot be glued unchanged across the three actual
integer fibers above. Set alpha=B. All positive-part terms vanish,
whereas

    M-B/Gamma_2 = (7c-3l)V/4.                          (9)

Hence every parameter range

    3l/7<c<l/2

gives a strict failure of (8), simultaneously with (7), equal global
budgets, a rank-two positive continuous circuit, and genuine global
criticality. Equivalently the ordinary overlap inequality with
coefficient 3/4 fails for the global cap masses. The caps themselves
have not been replaced by separate arbitrary covers on each fiber.

Here is one entirely rational instance, valid for every d>=2:

    l=1, c=9/20, L=[-1/2,1/2]^(d-1),
    v(w)=w_1, epsilon=1/2, A=2.

The fiber masses and the cap-mass table are

                 H_0       H_+       H_-
    z=-1        11/20        0         2
    z= 0        47/20      29/20      29/20
    z= 1        11/20        2         0

Thus

    M=39/5,  B=69/20,  max depth=23/52,
    M-(9/4)B=3/80,
    Gamma_2-max depth=1/468,
    (sum_i A_i-M)/min_i A_i=17/23<3/4.                (10)

Every fiber mass is less than M/2=39/10. The three caps are all
oblique or horizontal original ambient halfspaces with the continuous
normal span and global activity proved above. Their boundaries are
null for mixed d-volume; the separate lower-bound proof also retains
all possible positive boundary mass in other halfspaces.

## 5. Scope

The profile coefficient in (8) uses effective dimension two even
when d>2, since there are three caps. The counterexample therefore
tests precisely the ordinary effective-cap-count profile, not merely
the full-dimensional ordinary Gamma_d bound. Its maximum 23/52 is
strictly ABOVE Gamma_d/2 for n=1, so this is not an OC counterexample.
It does not exclude a profile with the needed parity loss or a
descent argument under a below-target hypothesis.

The mechanism blocked by (9) is lossless aggregation of the ordinary
cap-profile theorem across one integer midpoint. The actual midpoint
fiber, shared affine cap thresholds, global equal budgets, absence
of heavy fibers, positive circuit, and true critical activity do not
by themselves justify that aggregation.

Exact diagnostic: `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_three_fiber_effective_profile_gluing_minkowski.py`.
The all-parameter paired-tail proof above is the certificate; finite
arithmetic checks are supplementary.
